newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes mixed on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes mixed on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mixed against the dollar on Wednesday on what traders said were swap deals prior to the forthcoming long weekend.
"The market sold dollars this morning, then dealers took profits and swapped ahead of the weekend," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 0.5 of a centavo softer at 7.9350/7.9400 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate was 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.9200/7.9240 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 3.8 centavos firmer at 7.9000/7.9050 per dollar.
Dealers noted that 48-hour contracts made during the session will not be settled until Monday, due to the forthcoming long weekend.
The tendency was thus to sell dollars in the same-day market and buy them back at 48 hours using pesos that can meanwhile be invested in the local money market.
Mexican markets will be closed on Friday for holiday in honor of 19th century President Benito Jurez.
A late fall of 9/32 in U.S. 30-year Tresury bonds, to yield 6.98 percent, may also have pared earlier gains by the peso, dealers said.
"I think some who had oversold bought back dollars later on. Furthermore, (U.S.) long bond yields were up and the Dow was still down," the trader added.
The Dow Jones pared losses in afternoon trade, off 0.44 percent at 6,866.35 points in late trade.

Dealers drew attention to the fact that although the peso gained considerable ground in early trade, the advance did not warrant an additional auction of dollar puts by the central bank, a measure used in the past to drain surplus dollars from the market.
